reviewer: coordinator plus independent Luna recipe/API/packet review
instance_scope: One focused actual-Flow scenario proving selected Work/Walk/Wait handling and a named bed claim held through a caller-supplied cleaning completion callback, exact accepted release command and applied release event, with one queued request admitted afterward.
interface_contract: Implement only a crate-private calibration adapter in crates/kairo-ecs-calibration/src/staff_flow_lifecycle.rs and its private declaration in src/lib.rs. Connect the accepted select_dispatch result to caller-supplied Flow RequestId/EntityId/ResourceId/WorkId mappings without numeric casts. Keep Work, Walk and Wait as distinct typed activities; Work and Walk may submit distinct mapped requests, and Wait creates no request or claim. Model a named bed claim with explicit claim/owner/resource/request/lease identity and staged staff-versus-bed allocation, never atomic multi-resource acquisition. The fixture must schedule a caller-supplied cleaning domain callback for the same work/claim and bind its actual EventId. Keep the bed allocated and next request queued until the matching callback runs and its FlowBatchReceipt is Accepted with the exact emitted release ticket/event; step that actual release event before asserting release and queued admission. Assert request/owner/resource/lease lineage, callback and release EventIds, queue/resource conservation, and that wrong callback identity or rejected receipt cannot release the bed. Do not introduce cleaning duration/trigger policy, cancellation/expiry/conflict/failure policy, clinical semantics, public API, Cargo feature, DES/ABM core edits, or changes to accepted selector/transit modules.

verification.oracle: One or more focused lifecycle tests are selected and pass on stable Rust 1.99.0, including exact accepted callback/release-event lineage and held-bed/queued-request conservation. Record the nonzero selected test count and complete stdout/stderr log hash.
